chunks: From him, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who said: 'If an event befalls me during this illness, then my slave so-and-so is free.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'He may revoke from his will whatever he wishes and validate whatever he wishes.'
ai.seo_question: Can a person change or revoke their will after writing it?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the principle of absolute revocability (ruju') in wills is affirmed, allowing the testator to modify or confirm any portion of their disposition during their lifetime. Specifically addressing the manumission of a slave, the Imam clarifies that the testator is not bound by the initial declaration but retains full discretion to revoke or validate the bequest, reflecting the flexibility inherent in Shia jurisprudence regarding testamentary freedom.
